title: Toward an Explainable Early Warning Framework for Project Governance Using Organizational Project Portfolio Data
content: The analysis examines how historical project data can be used to identify factors associ-ated with project schedule delays and to support the development of an explainable Early Warning Framework. The analysis is based on data from 83 completed projects in a me-dium-sized IT service organization. After data preprocessing and descriptive analysis, Classification and Regression Trees (CART) were used to identify combinations of pro-ject-management conditions related to schedule performance. The resulting classification structure highlighted several factors associated with delays, including missed interim deadlines, communication and coordination problems, delayed responses to issues, diffi-culties in estimating work scope, and planning-related factors. The results are not intend-ed to represent a validated real-time prediction model. Instead, the identified decision rules provide an interpretable starting point for developing a prospective Early Warning Framework that combines historical organizational knowledge, explainable analytics, managerial review, and organizational learning. Further prospective testing is needed to assess whether these rules can provide sufficient predictive accuracy and lead time to support practical project governance.
